This guide will help you:

- [Update your Next.js application from version 12 to version 13](#nextjs-version)

## Upgrading

### Node.js Version

The minimum Node.js version is now **v18.17**. See the [Node.js documentation](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v18.x/api/) for more information.

### Next.js Version

To update to Next.js version 13, run the following command using your preferred package manager:

```bash package="pnpm"
pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
```

```bash package="npm"
npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
```

```bash package="yarn"
yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
```

```bash package="bun"
bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
```

### ESLint Version

If you're using ESLint, you need to upgrade your ESLint version:

```bash package="pnpm"
pnpm add -D eslint-config-next@latest
```

```bash package="npm"
npm install -D eslint-config-next@latest
```

```bash package="yarn"
yarn add -D eslint-config-next@latest
```

```bash package="bun"
bun add -D eslint-config-next@latest
```

events.content:
Every route is now on the App Router, the `pages/` directory is gone, and all the new code is TypeScript. The production build, type check and a smoke test against the running server all pass.

**What replaced what:**
- **`_app.js` + `_document.js`** → `app/layout.tsx`. It has the header, nav, footer, `lang="en"`, and the site description and favicon as `metadata`. The Google Fonts `<link>` is replaced by `next/font/google` (Inter), and `styles/globals.css` now uses `var(--font-inter)`.
- **`components/AppProvider.js`** → `AppProvider.tsx`, marked `'use client'`, with a typed context and `Theme` type.
- **`next/head`** → `metadata` exports, or `generateMetadata` for the blog post page.
- **`next/router`** → `useRouter` from `next/navigation`, in two small client components: `NavigateButton` (for `router.push`) and `BackButton` (for `router.back`). Internal `<a>` links are now `next/link`.
- **`index.js` (`getServerSideProps`)** → a Server Component in `app/page.tsx`. It reads the user agent with `await headers()` and fetches with `cache: 'no-store'`.
- **`blog/index.js` (`getStaticProps` with `revalidate: 60`)** → `app/blog/page.tsx` with `export const revalidate = 60`.
- **`blog/[id].js`**:
  - `getStaticPaths` → `generateStaticParams`, which pre-renders the first 10 posts.
  - `fallback: 'blocking'` → `dynamicParams = true`.
  - `revalidate: 300` stays as a 5-minute revalidate.
  - `notFound: true` → `notFound()`.
  - `params` is awaited and typed with `PageProps<'/blog/[id]'>`.
  - `router.isFallback` has no equivalent and was dropped. With `'blocking'` it never showed anyway, and adding a `loading.tsx` made unknown posts return 200 instead of 404, so I left it out.
- **`404.js`** → `app/not-found.tsx`, with its own metadata.
- **`_error.js` (`getInitialProps`)** → `app/error.tsx` plus `app/global-error.tsx`. They're client components using the `retry` prop, which is what this Next version (16.4 canary) documents in place of `reset`.
- **`pages/api/posts`** → Route Handlers in `app/api/posts/route.ts` and `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts`. They use `Response.json` and `await request.json()`, typed with `RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>`. The manual 405 branches are gone because Next now returns 405 for unsupported methods itself.
- **New `lib/posts.ts`**: typed `Post` and `Comment` models plus fetch helpers that check `res.ok`. That check is what lets a missing post correctly show the 404.

**Verification:**
- `npx next typegen` generated the route types.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passed (exit 0).
- `npx next build` passed (exit 0). `/` renders on each request, `/blog` refreshes every 1 minute, and `/blog/1` to `/blog/10` are pre-built and refresh every 5 minutes.
- Against `next start`:
  - `/`, `/blog`, `/blog/1` and `/blog/50` returned 200 with the right titles.
  - `/blog/99999` and `/nope` returned 404 with the custom not-found page.
  - On the API: GET 200, POST 201, POST without title/content 400, PUT 200, DELETE 200, and PATCH 405.
- I didn't trigger the error pages at runtime.

**Other changes to know about:**
- `npx next typegen` reformatted `tsconfig.json` and added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`. `next dev` would do the same.
- I added `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts` to `.gitignore`.
- The old files were removed with `git rm`, so those deletions are staged. Nothing was committed.
- The favicon is still referenced at `/favicon.ico`, but the project has no `public/` folder, just as before.
